The next experiment should verify that the generated predictor reproduces the selected BERT4Rec checkpoint before changing its learning objective. At 20% progress, deployment consistency is a feasible prerequisite for interpreting subsequent validation changes.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, all 14,148 audited supervised positions contained MASK, but original corruption provenance was unavailable in those measurements. Mask presence therefore does not certify event alignment. Second, 800 live identity checks passed. These compare executions of the live module and leave serialization, item mapping and category routing unchecked. Third, substitutions damaged training-prefix recovery more than block swaps. This supports content dependence on those fixtures, without establishing current usefulness or held-out gains.

Three related-work insights identify practical directions. RecTools explicitly reserves space for an appended inference MASK, motivating comparison of prepared tensors across execution paths [1]. PyTorch documents state-dict restoration and evaluation mode, providing concrete deployment checks [2]. Model-level metamorphic testing motivates candidate and batch permutation relations, whose applicability must be checked for this predictor [3].

| Direction | Existing evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision integrity | Consumed-batch reconstruction proposal | Bounded coverage and historical loss capture |
| Deployment consistency | Live identity checks | Actual generated predictor execution |
| Learning alignment | Training recovery sensitivity | Terminal prediction and pinned validation |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Generated-predictor differential audit: 4/8/5.** Originality: connects existing checks across the actual writer boundary, but differential testing is established. Potential: makes later experiments interpretable, but parity alone cannot improve ranking. Difficulty: requires no network changes, but routing and item-ID translation need careful integration [1–3].
- **Fixed terminal-mask training mixture: 4/8/4.** Originality: directly adapts a known objective mismatch, but terminal masking is established. Potential: may improve inference alignment, but benchmark gains are unknown. Difficulty: changes only sampling, but loss normalization and target-event exclusion require care [4].
- **Interior–terminal gradient comparison: 5/6/6.** Originality: adapts gradient-conflict analysis, but cosine disagreement is familiar. Potential: may localize interference, but cannot establish harmful transfer. Difficulty: reuses one network, but extra backward passes consume budget [5].

Select the differential audit. Freeze a small fixture suite per category containing short, full-length and repeated-item histories. Compare the live selected checkpoint against the actual generated `working/predict.py` in an isolated process: ordered external candidates, mapped IDs, prepared tokens, final-MASK readout and scores. Check strict checkpoint loading, candidate permutation and duplicate-candidate consistency. Report discrepancies, denominators and unavailable internals; use fixed dtype-specific tolerances and report near-tie ranking changes separately.

Calibrate on copied artifacts with independently verified wrong-route and wrong-readout faults. Preserve exactly one trained checkpoint per category. Retain diagnosis interfaces and use only pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 for model selection. No deployment parity or accuracy improvement has yet been measured.

idea.description: Add a bounded differential audit that compares the selected live BERT4Rec model with the actual generated working/predict.py loading that exact category checkpoint, including preparation, item mapping, routing and candidate scores.
idea.motivation: Consumed-batch provenance and live-module identity checks leave the exported prediction path uncertified. Establishing bounded deployment consistency makes subsequent sampler and loss experiments easier to interpret without adding another trained predictor.
idea.implementation_notes: This is an integration proposal because the baseline trainer, predictor writer and callable prediction interface were not supplied. Exercise the actual generated predictor in an isolated process; do not create a parallel reference predictor that bypasses the writer. Freeze training-history-only fixtures and ordered real-item candidate IDs before execution, covering unequal left padding, short histories, maximum-length histories and repeated items. Compare external-ID round trips, category/checkpoint identity, strict state-dict loading, configuration, prepared tensors and scores. Require reserved appended MASK inference and greatest-nonpadding absolute readout, never count-1. Intermediate checks require optional observation hooks that do not modify scoring; otherwise return null with reasons. Predeclare dtype-specific score tolerances, report maximum errors and rank differences near ties, and require exact equality for discrete IDs and tokens. Calibrate wrong-route and wrong-readout detectors using isolated copies with independently verified non-equivalent mutations; record inapplicable and unresolved cases separately. Missing runner support means unavailable, never passed. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView hooks. The probe must not advance the production loader or consume training RNG. Preserve four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per completed epoch. Keep single-GPU execution and exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category; live/reloaded executions share identical weights and are never fused. Preserve the twenty designated users' full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Bound audit execution within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects model revisions; audit fixtures provide no held-out accuracy estimate.
idea.pseudocode:
def audit_generated_predictor(view, runner, fixtures, checkpoint_manifest):
    if runner is None:
        return unavailable('No runner for the actual generated predictor')
    state = capture_module_modes_and_main_process_rng()
    try:
        view.model.eval()
        rows = []
        for fixture in fixtures:
            # Fixture contains public training history and ordered external candidates.
            live = observe_actual_training_side_prediction(view, fixture)
            exported = runner.predict_in_isolated_process(
                generated_file='working/predict.py',
                manifest=checkpoint_manifest,
                fixture=fixture,
                optional_observation_hooks=True)
            rows.append(compare_exact_discrete_fields_and_available_scores(
                live, exported, tolerances=PREDECLARED_DTYPE_TOLERANCES))
            rows.extend(check_candidate_permutation_and_duplicate_relations(
                runner, fixture, checkpoint_manifest))
        controls = calibrate_on_copied_artifacts(
            operators=['wrong_category_route', 'count_minus_one_readout'],
            require_independently_verified_non_equivalent_fault=True)
        return summarize_with_counts_definitions_and_unavailable_reasons(rows, controls)
    finally:
        restore_module_modes_and_main_process_rng(state)

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        result = existing_family_safe_diagnostics_without_production_iteration()
        result.update(audit_generated_predictor(
            self.view, optional_actual_export_runner(),
            frozen_training_only_fixtures(), selected_checkpoint_manifest()))
        return result  # Contains metrics and metric_definitions.

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish=['supervision_integrity', 'deployment_consistency',
                     'training_recovery', 'host_validation'],
        prohibit=['unmeasured_passes', 'invented_accuracy_gains', 'ensembles'])

originality.positive: Connects event-level integrity work to the actual predictor-writer, routing and serialization boundary under BERT4Rec semantics.
originality.negative: Differential testing, metamorphic relations and controlled fault injection are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable deployment evidence for later architecture, sampling and objective experiments.
future_potential.negative: Passing bounded fixtures cannot certify every prediction path or demonstrate improved recommendation relevance.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no new learned parameters, training objective or independently fitted scorer.
code_difficulty.negative: The actual generated predictor needs an isolated runner and optional observation hooks, with careful mapping and routing checks.

related_work.title: [1] RecTools BERT4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for left padding, history truncation and appended-MASK inference.
limitations: Does not establish correctness or parity of the supplied host implementation.

related_work.title: [2] PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents state-dict restoration and evaluation-mode requirements.
limitations: Successful parameter restoration alone does not verify preprocessing, item mapping or category routing.

related_work.title: [3] Model-level metamorphic-testing research (supplied search result)
contributions: Motivates checking equivalent executions through predefined metamorphic relations.
limitations: The proposed BERT4Rec relations require task-specific applicability checks; arbitrary padding shifts need not preserve absolute-position representations.

related_work.title: [4] Recency Sampling for Neural Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Identifies weak correspondence between masked reconstruction and terminal next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish that a terminal-mask mixture improves the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [5] Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Provides a framework for examining conflicting objective gradients.
limitations: Applying gradient comparisons to interior and terminal BERT4Rec objectives is a proposed adaptation; disagreement alone does not demonstrate harmful transfer.
